what_its_for: Levalbuterol is a bronchodilator (airway opener) used to treat and prevent wheezing, shortness of breath, and breathing problems caused by asthma or other lung conditions like COPD. It works by relaxing the muscles around your airways so air can flow more easily in and out of your lungs.
how_to_take: For the INHALER (HFA): Shake the inhaler well for at least 5 seconds before each use. Remove the cap and breathe out fully. Place the mouthpiece in your mouth and seal your lips around it. Press down on the inhaler as you breathe in slowly and deeply. Hold your breath for 10 seconds, then breathe out slowly. If you need a second puff, wait 1 minute before repeating. Rinse your mouth with water after use. For the NEBULIZER: Pour the liquid from the vial into the nebulizer cup. Breathe in the mist through the mouthpiece or mask for about 5 to 15 minutes until the nebulizer stops making mist. Prime a new inhaler by spraying 4 test puffs into the air before first use, or if you have not used it for more than 3 days.
dosing: Adults and children 12 and older: Inhaler - typically 1 to 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Nebulizer - usually 0.63 mg to 1.25 mg three times a day, about every 6 to 8 hours. Children 6 to 11 years: Nebulizer - usually 0.31 mg three times a day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different based on your needs.
missed_dose: If you use levalbuterol on a regular schedule and miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at one time. If you use levalbuterol only as needed (for sudden breathing problems), take it right away when symptoms start.
storage: Store the inhaler at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, open flame, and direct sunlight. Do not puncture or throw the canister into a fire. Store nebulizer vials at room temperature and protect them from light. Keep unused vials in the foil pouch until ready to use. Once you open a vial, use it right away. Keep all medications out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking or being around secondhand smoke, as it can make your breathing worse. Avoid known asthma or breathing triggers such as dust, pollen, pet dander, mold, and cold air. Do not use more puffs or doses than your doctor prescribed. Avoid taking other stimulant medications without asking your doctor first. Limit or avoid caffeine (coffee, energy drinks) as it may increase side effects like a fast heartbeat or shakiness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if: your breathing gets worse or does not improve after using this medication, you need to use it more often than prescribed, you have chest pain or a very fast or pounding heartbeat, you feel very shaky or dizzy, you have a serious allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face or throat, trouble breathing), your rescue inhaler is not helping during an asthma attack. Call your doctor if you have new or worsening symptoms, or if you are using this medication more than 2 days per week for symptoms.
when_it_works: Levalbuterol starts working quickly, usually within 5 to 15 minutes after you use it. Its effects typically last for 4 to 6 hours. It is a rescue medication, meaning it works fast to relieve sudden breathing symptoms. It is NOT a long-term controller medication and will not prevent asthma attacks if used alone over time.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using levalbuterol if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It may be used if benefits outweigh risks, but your doctor will guide you. Children: The nebulizer form is approved for children as young as 6 years old. Children under 4 should not use the HFA inhaler without specific doctor guidance. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as a fast heartbeat or tremors. Start with the lowest effective dose. Heart conditions: Use with caution if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, or an irregular heartbeat. Diabetes: Levalbuterol may raise blood sugar levels; monitor blood sugar closely if you have diabetes.
